q: According to the PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition, a project is best described as:
options: Ongoing work that sustains the organization
A temporary initiative in a unique context undertaken to create value
A collection of work managed as a group to achieve strategic objectives
Any work that takes less than one year to complete
explanation: A project is temporary, takes place in a unique context, and exists to create value. Ongoing work is operations, and duration alone does not define a project.

q: A company processes employee payroll every month using the same procedure. This work is best classified as:
options: A project
A program
Operations
A portfolio
explanation: Payroll is ongoing and repetitive with no planned end, which makes it operations.

q: In the definition of a project, what does 'temporary' mean?
options: The project work has a defined beginning and end
The deliverables will not last beyond the project
The project is short in duration
The project team is made up of contract staff
explanation: Temporary refers to the work having a start and a finish. Projects can last years, and their deliverables often persist long after the project ends.

q: Two project teams are each building an identical warehouse design, one in a coastal city and one in a mountain town, with different suppliers, regulators and stakeholders. Why are these considered two different projects?
options: Because they have different project managers
They are not; identical designs make them one project
Because warehouses are always unique products
Because each is carried out in a unique context
explanation: Unique context covers differences in location, resources, risks, stakeholders and other conditions, even when the goal is the same. It is why each project needs a tailored approach.

q: Which of the following is NOT a normal reason for a project to end?
options: The project's objectives have been achieved
The need for the project no longer exists because strategy changed
Funding is exhausted or no longer available
The project deliverables have been handed over and are now in routine daily use for five years
explanation: A project ends when objectives are met or cannot be met, resources are gone, the need disappears, or it is terminated. Years of routine use of the deliverable is operations and happens after the project already ended.

q: An organization is building a new airport. Separate projects for the runway, terminal, control tower and baggage system are managed in a coordinated way, because the benefit only appears when all of them work together. This is an example of:
options: A portfolio
A program
Operations
A project phase
explanation: Related projects managed in a coordinated manner to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually form a program.

q: Which activity is most characteristic of portfolio management?
options: Selecting and prioritizing programs and projects in line with strategic goals
Sequencing the activities of one project
Coordinating dependencies between related projects to create synergy
Running the daily production line efficiently
explanation: Portfolio management selects, prioritizes, manages and optimizes programs and projects against strategy. Coordinating related projects is program management.

q: Project management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities in order to:
options: Meet or exceed the intended value
Finish within budget regardless of the result
Deliver as many features as possible
Remove all risk from the project
explanation: The 8th edition definition is centered on the intended value. It explicitly does not endorse gold plating or scope creep.

q: A developer adds an extra reporting screen that the customer never requested, believing it will impress them. This is an example of:
options: Exceeding the intended value
Gold plating
A disbenefit
Tailoring
explanation: Adding unrequested extras is gold plating. 'Meeting or exceeding value' means value-driven decisions, not extra scope.

q: A project delivers a new online ordering system. Order processing costs fall by 20%, but several long-time customers who prefer phone orders leave. The loss of those customers is best described as:
options: An output
An artifact
A requirement
A disbenefit
explanation: Outcomes can be positive or negative. Positive ones are benefits; negative consequences or losses are disbenefits.

q: How does the PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition, define value?
options: The total amount of money the project earns
The number of deliverables completed
The satisfaction of the project sponsor
The excess of financial and non-financial benefits over the investment
explanation: Value is benefits (financial and non-financial) minus investment. Different stakeholders perceive it differently.

q: A project finished far over budget and years late, but its result became hugely popular and delivered benefits well beyond what was expected. How should its success be assessed?
options: It was a complete failure because the constraints were missed
It was a complete success because the outcome was good
The outcomes were successful, but the project management was not
Success cannot be assessed until the product is retired
explanation: Success has two dimensions: project outcomes (effectiveness in realizing value) and project management (efficiency against cost, scope, time and quality). They are assessed separately. The Sydney Opera House is the book's example.

q: In a value delivery system, what do programs and projects pass on to operations?
options: Deliverables, with support and maintenance information
Portfolio performance information
The organization's strategy
The desired outcomes, benefits and value
explanation: Strategy comes from senior leadership, desired outcomes come from portfolios, and programs and projects hand deliverables with support information to operations.

q: A project will hand its new system to an operations team at the end. When is the best time to involve that operations team?
options: At handover, so they are not distracted earlier
Early, during project planning
Only if problems appear after go-live
After the project is formally closed
explanation: Engaging operations teams early in planning strongly influences the long-term success and sustainability of the project's results.

q: Which of these is an example of intangible business value?
options: Market share
Monetary assets
Brand recognition
Infrastructure capabilities
explanation: Intangible examples include goodwill, brand recognition, reputation, acquired knowledge and employee well-being. Market share, monetary assets and infrastructure are tangible.
